question: Which ethical principle guides triage nurses to treat every patient fairly, no matter their background?

options.A: Autonomy
options.B: Paternalism
options.C: Justice
options.D: Beneficence

explanation: Justice means treating everyone fairly and sharing our healthcare resources impartially, without any bias or favoritism.

question: Which types of viral hepatitis are usually caught through the fecal-oral route?

options.A: Hepatitis B and E
options.B: Hepatitis B and C
options.C: Hepatitis A and E
options.D: Hepatitis C and D

explanation: Great job remembering this! Hepatitis A and E usually enter the body when someone consumes food or water that has been contaminated due to poor sanitation.

question: A gifted child gets extremely upset over loud noises or small unfairness in class. What explains this?

options.A: Oppositional defiant tendencies
options.B: Sensory and emotional overexcitabilities
options.C: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder
options.D: Typical delayed impulse control

explanation: Gifted kids often feel the world with extra intensity! Their nervous systems pick up on sounds, sights, and feelings much more strongly than others. Well done!

question: A patient experiences deep sadness after having a leg amputated. How should the nurse best view this emotional reaction?

options.A: A temporary phase of confusion caused by surgery
options.B: A sign of physical pain mistakenly labeled as sadness
options.C: An abnormal psychiatric disorder requiring immediate medication
options.D: A normal grief response to the loss of a body part

explanation: Grief is not restricted to death; patients can grieve functional losses like losing a limb or independence. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T8#GNS321_U4_T8_h1)

question: Why do fat-soluble drugs often get absorbed right back into the bloodstream from the kidney tubules?

options.A: Water pushes the drug molecules away from the urine exit channels.
options.B: Glomerular filtration fails to catch fat-soluble molecules the first time.
options.C: The kidneys actively try to keep all fat-soluble medicines inside the body.
options.D: Cell membranes easily let fat-soluble substances pass right back through them.

explanation: Think of cell membranes as being made of fatty layers. Because of this, fat-soluble drugs easily slip right back across them into the blood instead of staying in the urine to leave the body.

question: When should a nurse apply standard precautions in clinical practice?

options.A: Whenever a patient displays symptoms of an active fever
options.B: Exclusively in intensive care units and surgical theaters
options.C: Only when caring for patients with confirmed airborne diseases
options.D: For all patients receiving care, regardless of their diagnosis

explanation: Standard precautions are the baseline level of infection control used for every single patient interaction to prevent blood and fluid exposure. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T81#GNS214_U1_T81_h6)

question: Why is communication evaluated right alongside clinical nursing skills?

options.A: Soft skills replace the need for formal nursing board examinations
options.B: Clinical skills are entirely separate from how a nurse talks to patients
options.C: Communication scores are the only data required by insurance companies
options.D: Nursing requires effective teamwork and clear handovers to keep patients safe

explanation: Even if you are great at procedures, nursing is a team sport. Clear handovers and warm patient communication are vital to prevent mistakes.

question: How do sperm travel upward through the long vas deferens during ejaculation?

options.A: By beating their flagella very rapidly
options.B: By suction created by the prostate gland
options.C: By smooth muscle peristaltic contractions
options.D: By gravity pulling them down into the urethra

explanation: Just like food moves down your gut, the walls of the vas deferens use wave-like muscle squeezes (peristalsis) to push sperm smoothly along their journey.

question: Which stinging insect leaves its barbed stinger and venom sac behind in human skin?

options.A: Hornet
options.B: Wasp
options.C: Honeybee
options.D: Fire ant

explanation: Great job! The honeybee's stinger is barbed like a hook, so it anchors firmly into the skin and tears away from the bee's body along with the venom sac.

question: Why are community informants and patent medicine vendors important for surveillance in Nigeria?

options.A: They help capture health events in rural areas far from formal clinics
options.B: They possess advanced laboratory equipment for testing blood samples
options.C: They write the official national epidemiological weekly bulletins
options.D: They are responsible for funding all primary health care centers

explanation: Many rural citizens visit local medicine vendors or traditional attendants first, making these community actors vital for early case detection. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h4)

question: Why is checking nutritional status such an important part of nursing care for HIV patients?

options.A: Vitamins are the only treatment needed for early-stage disease
options.B: Poor nutrition prevents the skin from absorbing medications
options.C: Dietary changes can completely cure the viral infection
options.D: Wasting syndrome and chronic diarrhea frequently threaten recovery

explanation: Spot on. Good nutrition keeps the immune system strong, while complications like wasting and diarrhea can quickly pull a patient down.

question: Why do we track urine output after a patient suffers a severe allergic reaction?

options.A: To check for a urinary tract infection
options.B: To measure how much drug is left in the body
options.C: To check if the patient drank enough water
options.D: To see if the kidneys are getting enough blood flow

explanation: Kidneys need good blood pressure to make urine. Tracking output is a clever way to check if vital organs are getting enough blood.

question: What is the most important approach when counseling a client on a tight food budget?

options.A: Scolding them for wasting money on fast food
options.B: Providing a rigid meal plan that cannot be changed
options.C: Insisting they buy only organic imported foods
options.D: Practicing active listening without judgment

explanation: Exactly! Listening without judgment builds trust and helps you truly understand your client's financial reality.

question: Which task is part of the relief distribution duties of disaster agencies?

options.A: Delivering food and temporary shelter to displaced persons
options.B: Writing new national laws for civil aviation safety
options.C: Setting interest rates for commercial business loans
options.D: Conducting routine dental checks in public schools

explanation: Relief distribution is all about meeting basic human survival needs—like food, clean water, and shelter—for people forced out of their homes. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T9#GNS315_U1_T9_h4)

question: Why is treating only the physical wounds of a rescued trafficking victim not enough?

options.A: The psychological and social scars require extensive care
options.B: Mental health issues are never linked to physical trauma
options.C: Physical wounds always heal completely on their own
options.D: Physical treatment is too expensive for local clinics

explanation: Trafficking leaves deep emotional scars and isolation, meaning these children need dedicated mental health support alongside medical care.

question: A patient comes in with a warm, swollen, and painful knee after light activity. What is most likely going on?

options.A: Complete cessation of local osteoclast activity
options.B: Rapid mineralization of the surrounding bone matrix
options.C: Local inflammation and fluid accumulation in the joint
options.D: Immediate formation of a hard bony callus bridge

explanation: Warmth, swelling, and pain are classic signs of inflammation and fluid buildup inside the joint space. Great clinical deduction!

question: What is a common sign that a female patient has too much androgen in her system?

options.A: Permanent drop in core body temperature
options.B: Excessive facial hair growth and acne
options.C: Extreme softening of the fingernails
options.D: Sudden loss of all body hair

explanation: High androgens stimulate oil glands and hair follicles, which frequently leads to breakouts and unexpected hair growth patterns.

question: How should the nurse position the patient immediately after the thoracocentesis is finished?

options.A: Lying flat on the affected side with no pillows
options.B: Lying on the unaffected side for a short period
options.C: Flat on their stomach with arms raised over their head
options.D: Sitting upright with both arms locked behind the back

explanation: Positioning the patient on their un-punctured side promotes expansion and helps seal the puncture site. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T17#GNS221_U2_T17_h6)

question: What is a major long-term risk for patients dealing with ongoing autoimmune inflammation and immunosuppression?

options.A: Increased risk of cardiovascular disease and infections
options.B: Complete regeneration of destroyed organ tissue
options.C: Permanent stabilization of normal blood pressure
options.D: Total immunity against all forms of cancer

explanation: Constant inflammation wears down blood vessels over time, and medicines that lower immunity leave patients more open to infections.

question: How many main tiers make up Nigeria's public healthcare system?

options.A: Three distinct levels of care
options.B: Five distinct levels of care
options.C: Two distinct levels of care
options.D: Four distinct levels of care

explanation: Think of Nigeria's health setup like a ladder with three steps: primary, secondary, and tertiary. Each level is built to handle specific types of health needs in our communities!

question: What makes Participatory Rural Appraisal (PRA) different from traditional surveys?

options.A: It focuses only on collecting numerical laboratory test results
options.B: It is conducted entirely by foreign experts without local input
options.C: It requires expensive computers and satellite internet connections
options.D: It actively involves community members in analyzing their own conditions

explanation: Well done! PRA puts the community in the driver's seat to evaluate their own challenges.

question: Why is it important to ask a patient about their job and workplace environment during a social history?

options.A: It helps calculate the exact monthly income of the patient
options.B: It determines how many days off work the patient needs
options.C: Certain jobs expose workers to toxins that cause chronic illness
options.D: It shows whether the patient enjoys their daily job duties

explanation: Well reasoned! Workplace exposures like dust, fumes, or heavy lifting often play a big role in lung or body pains.

question: Why do communicable diseases spread so quickly in crowded IDP camps?

options.A: Close living quarters and poor sanitation facilities
options.B: Frequent distribution of expired food supplies
options.C: Lack of available traditional herbal remedies
options.D: Mandatory daily group physical exercise routines

explanation: When people live very close together without proper toilets or clean water, infections spread easily from person to person.

question: During a breathing trial, your patient starts sweating heavily, using their neck muscles to breathe, and their heart rate shoots from 85 to 130 beats per minute. What should you do?

options.A: Stop the trial and resume previous ventilator support settings
options.B: Encourage the patient to keep trying because anxiety is normal
options.C: Administer a strong sedative medication to calm the patient down
options.D: Remove the endotracheal tube immediately to finish extubation

explanation: Whoops, they are struggling! These are red flags that the breathing trial is failing. Put the ventilator settings right back where they were and let the machine help them rest.

question: What is the single leading cause of maternal death worldwide?

options.A: Postpartum hemorrhage
options.B: Gestational diabetes
options.C: Malaria
options.D: Eclampsia

explanation: Severe bleeding after childbirth (PPH) is the number one global killer of new mothers. As a nurse, knowing how to spot and manage PPH is a total lifesaver!

question: Which complication is a primary concern during the vaginal delivery of a macrosomic infant born to a mother with diabetes?

options.A: Shoulder dystocia
options.B: Placental accreta
options.C: Uterine inversion
options.D: Rapid cervical closure

explanation: Macrosomia means the baby is very large, which frequently leads to the baby's shoulders getting stuck behind the maternal pubic bone during delivery. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T006#GNS226_U4_T006_h6)

question: What kind of data do you collect when you count clinic attendance numbers and disease tallies?

options.A: Quantitative data
options.B: Fictional data
options.C: Qualitative data
options.D: Financial data

explanation: Whenever you see numbers and amounts (like tally counts), remember that's quantitative data!

question: A clinic logs 95 babies for Pentavalent 1, but only 60 return for Pentavalent 3. What does this show?

options.A: A successful outreach campaign with no service delivery gaps
options.B: An excellent level of continuous retention in the immunization clinic
options.C: A high program dropout rate requiring immediate community follow-up
options.D: An oversupply of vaccines that requires immediate redistribution

explanation: Dropping from 95 down to 60 means many infants aren't completing their schedule. Time for some community tracking and follow-up!

question: What is the clinical term for heartburn?

options.A: Pyrosis
options.B: Peristalsis
options.C: Preeclampsia
options.D: Pruritus

explanation: Pyrosis is simply the medical word for that burning feeling in your chest caused by stomach acid splashing up. You've got this!

question: What is the best way to organize the body of a literature review?

options.A: By the alphabetical order of the authors' first names
options.B: By the physical weight of the textbooks referenced
options.C: By the exact length of each published journal article
options.D: By themes, trends, or logical subtopics

explanation: Structuring your paper by themes lets you easily compare what different authors say about the same specific subtopic.

question: Why is it important for a primary health nurse to understand local traditional health beliefs?

options.A: It proves that traditional practices are always superior to science
options.B: It allows the nurse to replace all modern medicine with herbs
options.C: It stops patients from ever visiting local herbalists
options.D: It helps build trust and improves cooperation with medical treatments

explanation: Respecting traditional views helps nurses bridge the gap between community practices and safe, evidence-based health care. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T12#GNS124_U5_T12_h5)

question: What is the most common type of uterine cancer?

options.A: Squamous cell carcinoma
options.B: Clear cell carcinoma
options.C: Uterine leiomyosarcoma
options.D: Endometrial adenocarcinoma

explanation: Brilliant! Endometrial adenocarcinoma makes up the vast majority of all diagnosed uterine cancers.

question: When taking a baseline reproductive health history, what should you include?

options.A: Childhood vaccination records
options.B: Daily dietary calorie and sodium intake
options.C: Menstrual patterns and obstetric history
options.D: Family history of cardiovascular disease only

explanation: Great job! A good reproductive history focuses on menstrual cycles, past pregnancies, and sexual health to understand the patient's baseline.

question: What is the folded outer layer of the brain called?

options.A: Cerebral cortex
options.B: Brainstem
options.C: Spinal cord
options.D: Cerebellum

explanation: The cerebral cortex is the outer layer of neural tissue folded into gyri and sulci to maximize brain cell surface area. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T23#GNS211_U3_T23_h1)

question: Which nursing action helps most with the social and emotional challenges of chronic epilepsy?

options.A: Focusing solely on medication dosages and ignoring emotional health
options.B: Isolating the patient from family to reduce external stress
options.C: Encouraging the patient to hide their diagnosis from employers
options.D: Providing counseling resources and addressing social stigma

explanation: Epilepsy carries a lot of societal stigma in many communities. Offering support, education, and counseling helps patients build confidence and live full lives. You've got this! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T12#GNS222_U4_T12_h8)

question: How many layers make up the standard triple packaging system for infectious substances?

options.A: Three layers
options.B: One layer
options.C: Two layers
options.D: Four layers

explanation: The system consists of a primary receptacle, secondary packaging, and an outer packaging layer working together. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T20#GNS122_U3_T20_h4)

question: When health systems face a 'double burden of disease', what two types of health challenges are they dealing with?

options.A: Surgical trauma and genetic deformities
options.B: Acute poisoning and chronic malnutrition
options.C: Communicable and non-communicable illnesses
options.D: Pediatric and geriatric psychological disorders

explanation: Nailed it! It means fighting infectious diseases (like malaria) while also managing lifestyle conditions (like hypertension) at the same time.

question: A cardiac monitor shows a high heart rate for a patient who is lying quietly in bed. What should you do next?

options.A: Unplug all the chest electrodes to stop the reading
options.B: Quickly give a strong heart medication
options.C: Assume the monitor is broken and turn off the alarm
options.D: Check the patient for pain, fever, or anxiety before reacting

explanation: Tachycardia can happen because of pain, stress, or fever—not just a machine error. Always investigate the clinical cause first. You're doing great!

question: What is the primary clinical goal of administering oxygen and nitroglycerin during an acute heart attack?

options.A: To balance myocardial oxygen supply and reduce heart workload
options.B: To stimulate the nervous system to increase blood circulation
options.C: To lower the patient's body temperature and prevent a fever
options.D: To permanently cure underlying coronary artery plaque buildup

explanation: During a heart attack, the heart muscle lacks oxygen. Nitroglycerin decreases the workload, and oxygen increases supply, helping save heart tissue from dying. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T13#GNS213_U1_T13_h4)

question: What are nutrients mainly known as in nursing care?

options.A: Caloric restrictions required for managing chronic weight loss
options.B: Chemical substances in food needed for body function and repair
options.C: Medical supplements prescribed only during surgical recovery
options.D: Artificial additives used to preserve packaged hospital meals

explanation: You got this! Nutrients are simply the useful components in our food that give our bodies energy and help us grow and heal every day.

question: Which of these is NOT a safe way to source or store eye medications in a resource-limited setting?

options.A: Buying products only from verified, licensed pharmacies
options.B: Keeping drops away from direct sun and heavy heat
options.C: Buying medications from roadside hawkers to save money
options.D: Checking the expiry date before every application

explanation: Never buy drugs from roadside vendors! They often sell fake, expired, or poorly stored medications that can ruin vision or cause dangerous eye infections.

question: What does domiciliary midwifery mainly involve?

options.A: Managing high-risk pregnancies exclusively at home
options.B: Operating private surgical maternity hospitals
options.C: Supervising traditional birth attendants only
options.D: Providing maternity care inside the client's home

explanation: Domiciliary simply means at home! A domiciliary midwife cares for mothers right inside their own homes.

question: Why do many patients forget to mention their herbal supplements during a medication history interview?

options.A: Herbal products dissolve instantly and leave no trace in the body
options.B: Hospital regulations strictly forbid talking about traditional medicine
options.C: Nurses never ask about home remedies during admission
options.D: They consider supplements to be harmless food items rather than real drugs

explanation: Patients often view herbs as 'just food' or natural, so it doesn't cross their minds to report them as medications. That's why we always have to ask!

question: Which organs are prioritized and receive redirected blood flow during early shock?

options.A: The kidneys and the stomach
options.B: The skin and the skeletal muscles
options.C: The liver and the intestines
options.D: The brain and the heart

explanation: The body's survival reflex constricts vessels in less vital areas like the skin and gut to ensure the brain and heart continue to receive oxygen. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T2#GNS112_U7_T2_h2)

question: A patient with ALS is having muscle weakness and wasting. Which part of the nervous system is mainly affected?

options.A: The myelin sheath of peripheral nerves
options.B: Upper and lower motor neurons
options.C: Dopamine receptors in the basal ganglia
options.D: Sensory nerve endings in the skin

explanation: ALS attacks the motor neurons that tell your muscles to move. When these cells weaken, the muscles waste away (atrophy). You are building fantastic clinical knowledge!

question: What happens when a community actively participates in planning its own local health programs?

options.A: The programs are more likely to succeed and last long-term
options.B: Western medicine is completely rejected by the villagers
options.C: The government stops funding public health services entirely
options.D: Nurses no longer need to work in rural health centers

explanation: When people help build a program, they take ownership of it, making it much more sustainable over time. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h4)

question: Which of these items is counted as a medical sharp?

question: What is a major financial reason that pushes struggling families to marry off young daughters?

options.A: Requirement for agricultural labor grants

question: Why do nurses clean a wound starting from the center and wiping outward?

options.C: It speeds up how fast the skin cells can multiply.
options.D: It prevents pushing bacteria from the surrounding skin back into the wound bed.

explanation: Think of the center as the cleanest zone. Wiping outward ensures you don't drag outside germs back into the healing tissue!

question: How does a memory lapse differ from a mistake in everyday nursing practice?

options.A: A lapse is a memory failure, whereas a mistake is a planning failure
options.B: A lapse happens during surgery, whereas a mistake happens in the ward
options.C: A lapse involves equipment, whereas a mistake involves medication
options.D: A lapse is intentional, whereas a mistake is always accidental

explanation: Think of it this way: a lapse is forgetting a step because you got distracted, while a mistake is following a faulty plan because of incomplete knowledge.

question: Why do nurses treat the family as a single unit of care?

options.A: Home life and family habits directly shape how well a patient recovers
options.B: Families pay all medical bills together
options.C: Government policies legally require home visits
options.D: It reduces hospital admissions in the district

explanation: Illness affects everyone in the home, and daily habits strongly influence healing. Looking at the whole picture helps us give better care!

question: How does cervical cancer usually develop over time?

options.C: It appears suddenly as a widespread systemic blood infection
options.D: It forms from scar tissue after normal childbirth

question: Why does chronic malaria lead to high rates of anaemia in pregnant women?

options.A: Malaria drugs stop platelets from forming.
options.B: It thickens blood plasma instantly.
options.C: It stops the kidneys from filtering waste.
options.D: The malaria parasite destroys red blood cells as it grows.

question: Why is it crucial to keep track of a patient's total daily dose of paracetamol (acetaminophen)?

options.A: It causes rapid kidney failure within an hour

options.C: Overdosing immediately stops breathing

question: Why are complex blood tests usually not needed to diagnose Guinea worm disease?

question: What is the primary purpose of food distribution systems?

options.A: Setting international trade tariffs on crops

options.D: Determining the retail price of imported meat

question: Why is pre-training essential for nurses who will use research checklists on the ward?

options.A: To teach them how to perform advanced surgical operations

question: What is the main goal of using aseptic technique in microbiology?

options.A: To prevent unwanted contamination of samples and workspaces

options.C: To make bacterial growth happen much faster
options.D: To permanently freeze living microorganisms

question: How can severe, long-term stress mess up a woman's normal monthly cycle?

options.A: It suppresses brain signals that release reproductive hormones

question: How do incident reporting systems help a hospital protect itself legally?

question: How does the growing baby and uterus contribute to constipation later in pregnancy?

question: An enlarged prostate gland that blocks urine flow from the bladder falls under which category of acute renal failure?

question: What is the core spiritual reason behind vegetarianism in many Hindu and Buddhist traditions?

options.A: Strict government mandates enforced by ancient rulers
options.B: Ahimsa, meaning non-violence toward all living creatures
options.C: The absence of livestock farming methods in early history
options.D: The belief that all animal proteins cause immediate physical disease

explanation: Ahimsa is the beautiful principle of avoiding harm to any living thing, which strongly guides plant-based eating habits in these traditions.

question: Which of these common items spoils easily if left outside the fridge in warm weather?

options.A: Dry white rice
options.B: Canned tomato paste

options.D: Fresh milk

question: Why must certain dangerous illnesses like yellow fever be reported immediately to national authorities?

question: A pregnant patient on insulin therapy tells the nurse she feels shaky, sweaty, and dizzy. What is the immediate nursing action?

options.A: Wait thirty minutes to see if symptoms resolve

options.C: Provide a fast-acting oral carbohydrate source

question: How often should you reposition an immobile neurological patient to protect their skin?

options.A: Only when requested

question: What is the main purpose of regular team conferences in home health care?

question: Where do focal onset seizures originate in the brain?

options.A: Across both brain hemispheres simultaneously

options.D: In the peripheral nerves of the limbs

question: Why must you turn an unconscious patient onto their side before cleaning their mouth?

options.A: To help them wake up quicker
options.B: To stop fluids from entering the airway
options.C: To reach their back teeth easily
options.D: To help them produce more saliva

question: What is the most frequent cause of heavy bleeding after an abortion?

options.A: Severe high blood pressure

question: What is the single best way to stop resistant germs from spreading between patients?

options.A: Keeping patient room windows completely sealed shut
options.B: Administering daily multivitamins to all visitors
options.C: Sprinkling chemical disinfectants on hospital floors hourly
options.D: Performing thorough hand hygiene before and after care

explanation: Never underestimate simple handwashing! It remains our number one defense against carrying germs from patient to patient.

question: Which type of inhaler needs a fast, forceful breath from the patient to work properly?

options.A: Metered-dose inhaler
options.B: Valved holding chamber
options.C: Dry powder inhaler
options.D: Standard nebulizer

explanation: Dry powder inhalers don't use a spray propellant. Instead, the patient's own quick, deep breath pulls the powder out and breaks it up so it can reach the lungs!

question: Which mental health condition is common in women experiencing flashbacks and severe anxiety linked to FGM trauma?

options.A: Schizophrenia
options.B: Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder
options.C: Obsessive-compulsive disorder
options.D: Bipolar disorder

explanation: Well done! PTSD happens when the mind struggles to process heavy physical and emotional trauma, leading to flashbacks and constant anxiety.

question: Which of these is NOT a typical challenge to health education in Nigeria?

options.A: Excessive availability of advanced medical equipment in every village
options.B: Poverty and economic constraints
options.C: Cultural and traditional beliefs regarding illness
options.D: Language barriers and low literacy rates

explanation: Advanced equipment is definitely not overflowing in rural clinics! Resource shortages are the real hurdle, making this option false.

question: What is the main purpose of doing a summative evaluation at the end of an advocacy campaign?

options.A: Choosing which medical supplies to buy for patients
options.B: Planning the very first community health meeting
options.C: Measuring final outcomes and results after completion
options.D: Negotiating salaries with hospital administrators

explanation: You got it! A summative evaluation looks backward at the very end to check if you actually hit your original goals.

question: When a patient has vulval varicosities, which other body part should you check as a nurse?

options.A: The whites of the eyes
options.B: The lower extremities
options.C: The upper chest wall
options.D: The palms of the hands

explanation: Since pelvic congestion flows downward, it's very common to see leg varicose veins or swollen ankles accompanying vulval veins. Always look at the whole picture!

question: When is the second medication safety check typically performed?

options.A: While preparing or pouring the medication
options.B: When removing the drug from the storage shelf
options.C: During the morning nursing handover meeting
options.D: After the patient has swallowed the pill

explanation: The second check happens during preparation to ensure the right drug and dose are being measured out correctly. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T2#GNS125_U4_T2_h5)

question: What is a major challenge nurses often face when providing palliative care in resource-limited settings?

options.A: An excess of high-tech equipment that overwhelms patients
options.B: Limited access to essential pain medications and specialized facilities
options.C: A complete absence of family involvement in patient care
options.D: Patients refusing all forms of basic nursing assessment

explanation: In many resource-constrained settings, getting a steady supply of pain relief like opioids can be tough. Nigerian nurses often have to be creative and strong advocates for their patients!

question: What is the main reason we preserve food?

options.A: To completely eliminate all vitamins from food items
options.B: To replace natural food colors with artificial dyes
options.C: To stop or slow down food spoilage and microbial growth
options.D: To make food taste significantly sweeter and saltier

explanation: Food preservation stops germs and chemical reactions from spoiling our meals, helping keep food safe to eat later!

question: What is the best and most reliable way to confirm a multiple pregnancy?

options.A: Maternal blood pressure
options.B: Ultrasound scan
options.C: Fundal height palpation
options.D: Stethoscope auscultation

explanation: Spot on! An ultrasound gives us a clear picture, letting us count the gestational sacs and heartbeats early on. Modern tech makes midwifery so exciting!

question: What are the three main building blocks of healthcare financing?

options.A: Revenue collection, risk pooling, and purchasing
options.B: Drug manufacturing, supply, and distribution
options.C: Budgeting, staffing, and facility management
options.D: Patient admission, treatment, and discharge

explanation: Think of healthcare financing like a cooperative thrift society: you collect money, pool the risk together, and buy what the group needs. These three steps keep health systems running!

question: When should you inspect the outside of the ear (the auricle)?

options.A: Only after the otoscopic examination is fully completed
options.B: While cleaning cerumen out of the middle ear space
options.C: Before inserting the speculum into the ear canal
options.D: Immediately after removing the pneumatic bulb attachment

explanation: Always check the outside of the ear first for any tenderness or sores before putting anything into the canal.

question: An elderly patient who lost their spouse recently won't speak and looks very withdrawn. What should you do first?

options.A: Provide a safe space for the patient and gently encourage expression of feelings
options.B: Ignore the withdrawal since it is expected after losing a spouse
options.C: Tell the patient that life goes on and they need to cheer up immediately
options.D: Transfer the patient to a psychiatric unit without further assessment

explanation: Listening with empathy and being present helps patients process grief safely without feeling rushed. Excellent nursing care!

question: How do patients usually move through the stages of dying?

options.A: Rapidly within the first twenty-four hours of a diagnosis
options.B: Always starting with depression and ending with anger
options.C: Fluidly, often moving back and forth or skipping steps
options.D: Strictly one after the other in a neat timeline

explanation: Grief is never a straight line. Patients often bounce back and forth or skip steps entirely, and that is completely normal!

question: What physical event causes a sudden rise in the newborn's systemic blood pressure?

options.A: Clamping of the umbilical cord
options.B: The baby crying for the first time
options.C: Closure of the foramen ovale
options.D: Contraction of the ductus arteriosus

explanation: Cutting the cord removes the low-resistance placenta, which sharply increases resistance and pressure in the systemic circulation. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T9#GNS121_U6_T9_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of conducting a physical stock audit on a hospital ward?

options.A: To test the clinical skills of newly employed nurses
options.B: To compare actual items on the shelf with recorded inventory
options.C: To clean out the dust from the medication store cupboards
options.D: To dispose of all old equipment regardless of expiry date

explanation: Stock audits involve counting what is physically present to match it with what the logbook says should be there. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h6)

question: A patient is admitted with severe heart failure and fluid accumulation in the lungs. Why is a low salt diet ordered?

options.A: To prevent further fluid retention and reduce cardiac workload
options.B: To improve digestion and absorption of oral medications
options.C: To stimulate red blood cell production in the bone marrow
options.D: To cure the underlying viral infection in the heart muscle

explanation: Restricting salt stops the body from holding onto extra water, which lessens the volume of blood the weakened heart has to pump. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T007#GNS227_U6_T007_h3)

question: Why do problems in the brain-testicle hormone pathway (hypothalamic-pituitary-testicular axis) often affect both sperm and testosterone?

options.A: Because the pituitary gland directly manufactures all male gametes
options.B: Because hypothalamic neurons physically transform into mature spermatozoa
options.C: Because testosterone is exclusively stored in the anterior pituitary gland
options.D: Because the axis controls both testosterone production and germ cell maturation

explanation: Think of the brain as the master switch that controls two main factories: Leydig cells for testosterone and Sertoli cells for sperm. When the master switch has issues, both processes are affected!

question: An older patient seems to be losing their hearing, but it's actually a simple, fixable blockage. What is it?

options.A: Cerumen impaction
options.B: Cochlear hair cell death
options.C: Tympanic membrane scarring
options.D: Auditory nerve atrophy

explanation: Cerumen impaction is just a fancy word for heavy earwax buildup! Once you clean it out, the patient's hearing usually pops right back to normal.

question: Your patient keeps trying to talk and laugh with food in their mouth. What should you do?

options.A: Keep pushing the next spoonful of food into the mouth quickly
options.B: Scold the patient firmly for bad table manners
options.C: Ask the patient to finish chewing and swallowing before speaking
options.D: Remove the food tray immediately and skip the meal

explanation: Friendly reminders work best! Gently asking them to swallow first keeps them safe from choking while keeping the mood warm.

question: What is the main job of aldosterone from the adrenal glands?

options.A: Lowering blood sugar after a heavy meal
options.B: Helping bones grow during puberty
options.C: Making the heart beat faster during fright
options.D: Managing salt and water balance in the kidneys

explanation: Correct! Aldosterone tells your kidneys to hold onto sodium and water, which keeps your blood pressure steady.

question: Which assessment is most important to keep checking for a patient in an oxygen tent?

options.A: Respiratory rate and work of breathing
options.B: Bowel sounds and abdominal circumference
options.C: Daily weight and fluid intake volume
options.D: Neurological reflex response scores

explanation: Since oxygen tents treat breathing problems, always keep a close eye on how hard the child is working to breathe and their breathing rate.

question: Why is proper post-harvest management important for food security?

options.A: It increases the chemical fertilizer content in staple grains
options.B: It removes the need for farmers to rotate their crops
options.C: It forces farmers to sell all their crops immediately after harvesting
options.D: It prevents food loss from pests and spoilage during lean periods

explanation: Correct! Storing and preserving food properly keeps it safe from pests so families have something to eat even when crops are scarce.

question: A patient with Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) is finding it hard to conceive. What is the main reason for this?

options.A: Complete blockage of both fallopian tubes
options.B: Severe narrowing of the lower vaginal canal
options.C: Premature shedding of the uterine lining
options.D: Failure to regularly release an egg during her cycle

explanation: Exactly! PCOS often messes with ovulation, meaning eggs aren't regularly released each month. Keep up the momentum!

question: Why is teaching a patient to keep a menstrual calendar a helpful nursing action?

options.A: It replaces the need for any further laboratory blood testing
options.B: It serves as a permanent medical cure for abnormal hormones
options.C: It completely prevents the future development of ovarian cysts
options.D: It empowers the patient to track cycle patterns and share accurate data with clinicians

explanation: Data is power! A calendar helps both the nurse and the patient see patterns clearly, spot changes early, and check if treatments are working.

question: A nurse is advising a low-risk traveler on where to stay during a 14-day observation period. Which option is most practical and commonly used?

options.A: Intensive care unit isolation room
options.B: Home quarantine with restricted movement
options.C: A high-security prison medical ward
options.D: The outpatient infectious disease clinic

explanation: For low-risk exposures without symptoms, home quarantine is the standard, practical approach to manage large numbers of people. [learn more](GST114_U2_T16#GST114_U2_T16_h3)

question: What is the main goal of vocational rehabilitation?

options.A: To teach basic hospital nursing procedures
options.B: To cure the underlying chronic disease process
options.C: To help individuals return to work or economic productivity
options.D: To provide permanent disability allowances without work

explanation: Vocational rehab is all about empowering people with skills so they can earn a living and stand firmly on their own feet financially.

question: Why do we use synthetic swab tips (like dacron) instead of regular cotton?

options.A: Synthetic swabs change color to indicate a positive infection
options.B: Cotton can inhibit certain laboratory tests and microbial growth
options.C: Synthetic tips are significantly cheaper to purchase in bulk
options.D: Cotton fibers dissolve completely when exposed to body fluids

explanation: Regular cotton can actually trap or stop germs from growing properly in the lab, so synthetic swabs give us much more reliable test results.

question: Which of these is a serious danger sign in pregnancy that means 'go to the clinic now'?

options.A: Vaginal bleeding at any stage of pregnancy
options.B: A slight increase in normal daily appetite
options.C: Mild fatigue after walking short distances
options.D: Mild morning nausea during the first trimester

explanation: Bleeding is never normal when expecting. It's always a warning sign that needs immediate medical evaluation to keep both mother and baby safe.

question: An increasing population of older adults in Nigeria will most likely lead to a higher demand for what service?

options.A: Management of chronic health conditions
options.B: Primary school infrastructure
options.C: Pediatric immunizations and infant care
options.D: Obstetric and maternity wards

explanation: Older populations experience higher rates of long-term illnesses like high blood pressure and diabetes, increasing the need for chronic care. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T1#GNS321_U3_T1_h2)

question: What does a low Height-for-Age measurement tell you about a child?

options.A: Temporary weight gain from eating too much sugar
options.B: Acute dehydration from recent diarrhea
options.C: Chronic malnutrition or stunting over a long period
options.D: Immediate lack of protein causing fluid swelling

explanation: Spot on! Height-for-age is our long-term scorecard. A low score tells us the child has been dealing with poor nutrition over a good while (stunting).

question: What exactly is a 'near miss' in clinical practice?

options.A: A minor medication reaction that needs no treatment
options.B: An error that is caught before it ever reaches the patient
options.C: A patient complaint about poor nursing communication
options.D: An adverse event that causes permanent patient disability

explanation: Brilliant! A near miss is when something could have gone wrong, but quick thinking or sheer luck stopped it just in time. No harm done!

question: How do operational expenses differ from capital expenses?

options.A: Operational expenses are optional, while capital expenses are legally required
options.B: Operational expenses are paid only once a decade, while capital expenses are paid daily
options.C: Operational expenses cover daily running costs, while capital expenses cover long-term major assets
options.D: Operational expenses involve patient care items, while capital expenses involve office furniture only

explanation: Operational costs keep the hospital running day by day, while capital costs are for big, long-lasting investments.

question: Which group of medications is usually given first to stop a long-lasting seizure?

options.A: Diuretics
options.B: Opioid analgesics
options.C: Beta-blockers
options.D: Benzodiazepines

explanation: Correct! Fast-acting benzodiazepines are the go-to emergency drugs to calm down runaway brain activity quickly.

question: What term describes how consistent and repeatable a research measurement tool is?

options.A: Randomization
options.B: External validity
options.C: Selection bias
options.D: Reliability

explanation: If a tool is reliable, you can trust it to give you consistent results every single time you use it, no matter who is holding it.

question: What is a major plus when you use seasonal food ingredients for a menu?

options.A: It guarantees that all meals will be completely fat-free
options.B: It removes all cultural restrictions from the meal plan
options.C: It completely eliminates the need for food preservation
options.D: It lowers food costs and guarantees ingredient freshness

explanation: In-season foods are harvested locally in plenty, making them cheaper and way fresher for the kitchen.

question: Why do people stopping heavy alcohol use often experience dangerous symptoms like shaking (tremors) and seizures?

options.A: The brain experiences a rebound effect of hyperexcitability
options.B: The liver fails to filter out toxins quickly enough
options.C: The stomach lining becomes irritated by lack of nutrients
options.D: The muscles lose all stored protein and water

explanation: Brilliant! Since alcohol depresses the brain, taking it away suddenly causes the nervous system to bounce back hard and become dangerously overactive.

question: What is the main sign you will notice in a patient with a vesicovaginal fistula?

options.A: Inability to pass any urine at all for several days
options.B: Passing bright red blood clots instead of normal urine
options.C: Severe sharp pain and burning sensation during urination
options.D: Continuous and uncontrollable leakage of urine from the vagina

explanation: Spot on! Because urine bypasses the normal valve completely, it leaks out constantly without the patient being able to hold it. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T12#GNS216_U5_T12_h1)

question: What does 'mesial temporal sclerosis' mean in temporal lobe epilepsy?

options.A: Scarring and neuron loss in the hippocampus
options.B: A sudden blockage of the carotid artery
options.C: Bleeding into the ventricles of the brain
options.D: Inflammation of the outer brain lining

explanation: Think of mesial temporal sclerosis as scarring deep inside the temporal area (the hippocampus). This damage makes it easier for abnormal electrical storms to start. Keep pushing forward! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T12#GNS222_U4_T12_h1)

question: Which finding in a patient's urine test often makes a doctor request an IVP?

options.A: Blood (hematuria)
options.B: White blood cells
options.C: Excess protein
options.D: Glucose

explanation: Spotting blood in the urine (hematuria) is a major clue that prompts doctors to use an IVP to check for stones, tiny growths, or injuries inside.

question: You touch a hot pot in the clinical kitchen and instantly pull your hand back. Which fibers carried the signal from your CNS out to your hand muscles?

options.A: Sensory fibers
options.B: Efferent fibers
options.C: Receptor fibers
options.D: Afferent fibers

explanation: E-fferent exits the brain with instructions (think 'E' for exit). Quick reflexes keep future nurses safe! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T2#GNS211_U3_T2_h4)

question: What is a major risk of pushing a client too early into regular open employment?

options.A: Permanent immunity from all future mental health challenges
options.B: Sudden loss of physical mobility in the upper limbs
options.C: High anxiety, job failure, and potential psychiatric relapse
options.D: Immediate promotion to a senior executive board position

explanation: Pushing a client into a regular job before they are ready can overwhelm them and undo their hard-earned progress. Fantastic work completing today's session!

question: What happens during passive health surveillance?

options.A: The government bans the collection of all health statistics
options.B: Nurses actively hunt for sick people in every single household
options.C: Patients diagnose themselves at home without telling anyone
options.D: Clinics routinely report disease cases upward to health authorities

explanation: In passive surveillance, we wait for patients to come to the clinic feeling unwell, and then our routine reports flow up to the health authorities. It's the standard way we track everyday illnesses!

question: A 20-month-old toddler comes to the clinic and their front fontanelle is still wide open. What condition might you suspect?

options.A: Craniosynostosis
options.B: Severe dehydration
options.C: Normal variant requiring no follow-up
options.D: Hypothyroidism or rickets

explanation: Great clinical thinking! When soft spots stay open longer than usual, it can point toward metabolic or bone issues like rickets or hypothyroidism.

question: Why does a teenage boy's voice crack and deepen?

options.A: Hypertrophy of the salivary glands from increased testosterone
options.B: Narrowing of the pharynx due to rapid facial bone growth
options.C: Elongation of the vocal cords due to laryngeal cartilage growth
options.D: Swelling of the tonsils caused by an upper respiratory infection

explanation: Well done! Testosterone makes the voice box (larynx) grow larger, stretching the vocal cords and dropping the pitch of the voice.

question: How does higher education generally help a person's diet?

options.A: It improves the ability to read food labels and spot hidden sugars
options.B: It eliminates the need to buy fresh fruits and vegetables
options.C: It guarantees that a person will never develop chronic illnesses
options.D: It stops people from eating processed foods completely

explanation: Education gives people the tools to evaluate food contents and make informed choices about what they eat. You are doing great!

question: What is the core belief behind quantitative research?

options.A: A single objective reality exists that can be measured
options.B: Reality is entirely subjective and changes for every person
options.C: Facts only matter if the patient agrees with the nurse
options.D: There is no truth, only personal opinions in healthcare

explanation: Quantitative research assumes there is a clear, measurable truth out there waiting to be discovered with the right tools.

question: What training tool is commonly used to help healthcare providers address personal biases toward abortion patients?

options.A: Mandatory pharmaceutical sales and marketing courses
options.B: Value clarification and attitude transformation workshops
options.C: Strict legal prosecution guidelines for nursing students
options.D: Advanced surgical training in abdominal hysterectomy

explanation: Well done! These workshops help staff examine their own beliefs and separate personal bias from their duty to save lives.

question: Why is a water-soluble lubricant used instead of an oil-based jelly on the tube?

options.A: Water-soluble jelly permanently stiffens the plastic tube
options.B: Oil-based lubricants make the tube too slippery to hold
options.C: Water-soluble jelly will not harm the lungs if accidentally inhaled
options.D: Oil-based products react badly with stomach acid

explanation: If the tube accidentally enters the trachea, a water-soluble lubricant is safely absorbed by lung tissue, unlike oils which cause lipid pneumonia. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T3#GNS213_U3_T3_h3)

question: Why do a community health assessment before starting a new health project?

options.A: It proves that the community has no existing health problems
options.B: It ensures interventions address the actual, specific needs of the population
options.C: It eliminates the need to ever speak with traditional leaders
options.D: It is a legal requirement that guarantees government funding approval

explanation: You don't want to guess what people need! Assessing first makes sure you are solving their real, everyday struggles.

question: Where should you put used, un-capped needles and syringes right after an injection?

options.A: Inside a regular black polythene trash bag
options.B: On top of the clean vaccine preparation tray
options.C: In a puncture-resistant safety box
options.D: In the patient's personal pocket or bag

explanation: Always drop used sharps straight into a safety box to protect yourself, your colleagues, and waste handlers from accidental pricks.

question: What is the main difference between latent TB and active TB disease?

options.A: Latent TB bacteria are dead, while active TB bacteria are alive.
options.B: Latent TB requires hospital admission, while active TB is treated at home.
options.C: Latent TB only affects children, while active TB only affects adults.
options.D: Latent TB has no symptoms and is not contagious, whereas active TB causes illness and spreads.

explanation: Think of latent TB as sleeping quietly in the body—the person feels fine and cannot pass it on. Active TB is awake, causing illness, and can spread to others.

question: You need to give a routine vaccine to a healthy 12-month-old baby. Which injection site is best?

options.A: Dorsogluteal
options.B: Ventrogluteal
options.C: Vastus lateralis
options.D: Deltoid

explanation: Spot on! The vastus lateralis (thigh muscle) is nice and plump in little infants, making it the go-to, safe spot for routine baby immunizations.

question: How should a domiciliary midwife track how labor is going during a home delivery?

options.A: By checking maternal blood pressure only once a day
options.B: By waiting until the baby cries before taking any measurements
options.C: By asking family members to guess the cervical dilation
options.D: By monitoring contractions, vital signs, and fetal heart rate regularly

explanation: Regular checks of the mother's vitals and the baby's heartbeat keep you ahead of any trouble and let you know everything is progressing well.

question: What is the main function of the Bartholin glands?

options.A: Release hormones that trigger puberty
options.B: Protect the pubic bone from physical shock
options.C: Secrete lubricating mucus into the vestibule
options.D: Produce eggs during the monthly cycle

explanation: Bartholin glands sit beside the vaginal opening and produce mucus to keep the mucosal surface moist. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T1#GNS216_U2_T1_h2)

question: What is the final active form of vitamin D made by the kidneys?

options.A: Ergocalciferol
options.B: Cholecalciferol
options.C: Cholesterol
options.D: Calcitriol

explanation: You're doing great! The kidneys put the finishing touch on vitamin D by turning it into calcitriol, which keeps your bones strong and healthy.

question: During a vaginal exam, you feel that the baby's skull bones are severely overlapping and jammed tight. What condition might this suggest?

options.A: Premature rupture of membranes
options.B: Normal rapid crowning
options.C: Normal painless descent
options.D: Cephalopelvic disproportion

explanation: Severe, tight overlapping is a sign that the head is struggling to fit through a tight birth canal—a condition we call cephalopelvic disproportion (CPD). Keep this red flag in mind for clinicals!

question: Why can sending random, unrequested donations by the public sometimes cause trouble during a disaster?

options.A: They violate international trade laws regarding tax exemptions
options.B: They clog ports and waste time sorting items that cannot be used
options.C: They reduce the funding available for local volunteer stipends
options.D: They automatically trigger a mandatory audit by the United Nations

explanation: Spot on! Well-meaning boxes of random clothes or expired goods end up blocking logistics hubs, wasting precious time when people need actual medical supplies.

question: A nurse manager wants to involve an experienced team of senior nurses in designing a new shift roster. Which style is best?

options.A: Autocratic
options.B: Laissez-faire
options.C: Coercive
options.D: Democratic

explanation: Democratic leadership welcomes staff input and collaboration, making it ideal for planning and problem-solving tasks. [learn more](GST321_U1_T13#GST321_U1_T13_h3)

question: How many separate bones are typically found in a healthy adult human body?
explanation: An adult human skeleton typically consists of 206 distinct bones after various smaller bones fuse together during childhood development. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T4#GNS121_U3_T4_h1)

question: Why would a nurse researcher choose a qualitative design over a quantitative one?

options.A: To calculate the exact statistical cost of hospital equipment
options.B: To measure the physical growth rate of pediatric patients
options.C: To understand the deep personal meaning of living with a chronic illness
options.D: To prove which medication cures a bacterial infection fastest

explanation: Qualitative research shines when we want to capture human emotion, personal perspectives, and lived experiences through words.

question: Why is a patient told not to eat or drink (NPO) before a laparoscopy?

options.A: To prevent the surgical instruments from getting dirty
options.B: To ensure the patient loses weight before surgery
options.C: To stop the kidneys from producing urine
options.D: To reduce the risk of aspiration during anesthesia

explanation: Spot on! Keeping the stomach empty stops food or vomit from flowing up and entering the lungs while the patient is fast asleep under anesthesia.

question: What is the most common nutritional problem facing adolescent girls in Nigeria today?

options.A: Pellagra from maize diets
options.B: Beriberi from polished rice
options.C: Iron-deficiency anemia
options.D: Scurvy from lack of citrus fruits

explanation: You got it! Iron-deficiency anemia is the top nutritional challenge for Nigerian teenage girls due to diet and monthly blood loss.

question: Which skin structure produces watery fluid to help cool the body through evaporation?

options.A: Subcutaneous fat cells
options.B: Eccrine sweat glands
options.C: Sebaceous glands
options.D: Arrector pili muscles

explanation: Great job! Eccrine sweat glands release water onto our skin, which cools us down as it evaporates into the air.

question: Why are anti-diarrhea drugs sometimes avoided when a patient has an infection causing their diarrhea?

options.A: Diarrhea helps the kidneys filter extra salt from the blood
options.B: Antibiotics are the only approved treatment for any diarrhea
options.C: These medications always cause permanent bowel paralysis instantly
options.D: Stopping stool too fast can trap harmful bacteria inside the body

explanation: Makes sense, right? Diarrhea is actually the body's way of flushing out bad germs. Shutting it down too quickly can trap those toxins inside.

question: At what specific time intervals is the Apgar score routinely assessed after birth?

options.A: Immediately and thirty minutes
options.B: Ten minutes and twenty minutes
options.C: Two hours and four hours
options.D: One minute and five minutes

explanation: The Apgar score is standardly evaluated at one minute to check how well the baby tolerated birth, and at five minutes to see how well the baby is adapting outside the womb. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T51#GNS214_U1_T51_h1)

question: Which nutrients are especially vital for a patient healing from a broken bone?

options.A: Calcium, vitamin D, and protein
options.B: Vitamin C and simple sugars
options.C: Sodium and complex starches
options.D: Iron and fluid electrolytes

explanation: Calcium and vitamin D make the bone hard and strong again, while protein builds the framework for the new tissue. Diet plays a huge role in recovery!

question: What is the main job of the sutures in a baby's skull during pregnancy and birth?

options.A: To allow flexibility and slight movement between the skull bones
options.B: To produce cerebrospinal fluid for the developing brain
options.C: To prevent blood from pooling inside the cranial cavity
options.D: To act as anchor points for the muscles of mastication

explanation: Exactly! These fibrous joints act like shock absorbers, letting the skull reshape smoothly as it moves through the pelvis.

question: Why is it risky to reuse old prescription drugs for a new sickness?

options.A: The current symptoms may stem from a completely different underlying condition
options.B: Old pills lose their physical shape and become impossible to swallow safely
options.C: Pharmacy laws strictly forbid keeping unused tablets in a home cabinet
options.D: Expired medications always turn into toxic chemical substances immediately

explanation: Just because malaria felt a certain way last month doesn't mean today's fever is malaria! Treating a new problem with old medicine can delay finding the real issue.

question: Which nerve-related symptom is commonly linked to a vitamin B12 deficiency?

options.A: Sudden paralysis on one entire side of the body
options.B: Severe sharp pain radiating down the lower back
options.C: Inability to recognize familiar faces or places
options.D: Tingling and numbness in the hands and feet

explanation: Vitamin B12 is super important for nerve health. When you don't have enough, your peripheral nerves get irritated, causing that classic tingling and numbness (paresthesia).

question: A patient says he reaches climax much faster than he wants during intercourse. What is he experiencing?

options.A: Hypoactive sexual desire disorder
options.B: Delayed ejaculation
options.C: Premature ejaculation
options.D: Erectile dysfunction

explanation: You nailed it. When ejaculation happens sooner than the man or his partner would like, it's called premature ejaculation.

question: Who belongs on the multidisciplinary team supporting a patient's psychosocial recovery?

options.A: Hospital accountants and administrative billing staff
options.B: Pharmacists and surgical instrument sterilization technicians
options.C: Psychologists, occupational therapists, and social workers
options.D: Security guards and hospital maintenance engineers

question: What is an important nursing action after giving an antagonist antidote like naloxone?

question: What is the main goal of the 'sensitivity' part of a urine culture and sensitivity (C&S) test?

question: Which of these actions should a nurse NOT take when dealing with unhelpful illness behaviour?

question: When is the right time to suction a patient who is on a ventilator?

question: What is a likely result of poor integration between different levels of hospital objectives?

question: Why do investigators use the 'Five Whys' technique during an incident review?

question: An infection control nurse sees more wound infections popping up on a surgical ward. What should be the first step?

question: Which Nigerian agency leads national disease tracking and outbreak responses?

question: When do you typically hook up a humidification bottle filled with sterile water to an oxygen setup?

question: How do inherited degenerative diseases usually progress compared to a sudden injury?

question: How does the medication hydroxyurea help treat sickle cell anaemia?

question: Why are good learning experiences so important for you as a nursing student?

question: What happens to a pregnant woman's resting heart rate?

question: Why is it super helpful for nurses to understand the whole chain of infection?

question: Why should you do a quick physical assessment right after the steam session ends?

question: How do modern smart-speaker voice assistants help someone with severe vision loss?

options.B: They allow hands-free control of timers, reminders, and information

question: A patient complains of sharp pain in their lower right tummy. Which organ should a nurse suspect right away?

question: A community health nurse in Nigeria is teaching mothers how to prevent childhood diarrhea. Which historical concept supports this health education?

question: What is the main goal of giving antiretroviral therapy (ART) to someone with HIV?

options.C: To prevent the transmission of common bacterial colds

question: Why is patient-centered care an important part of reproductive health quality?

options.B: It ensures mothers are treated with respect and dignity

question: What is the first thing a community health nurse should do when an unusual cluster of sick people appears?

question: What is the purpose of taking a plain x-ray of the abdomen before injecting the contrast dye?

question: What is an essential nursing responsibility before synovial fluid aspiration begins?

question: Why is it important to connect daily nursing tasks to the broader organizational goals?

question: How should you correctly measure the length of an infant?

question: Why do we combine two different drugs in Artemisinin-Based Combination Therapy (ACT)?

question: What type of grief occurs before an actual loss takes place, such as during a terminal illness diagnosis?

question: How do nurse-led community outreach programs help improve maternal health in rural Nigeria?

question: A hormone travels through the whole body, but why does it only affect certain cells?
